props.command: write a Manim scene showing: An attacker changes their Discord display name to 'Chris' — the agent's owner. The agent catches it: the user ID doesn't match. The name changed, the account didn't. Suspicious request refused. Then the attacker opens a n

beats.narration_text: An attacker changes their Discord display name to 'Chris' — the agent's owner. The agent catches it: the user ID doesn't match. The name changed, the account didn't. Suspicious request refused. Then the attacker opens a new private channel. The agent has no memory of the previous interaction. No record of the suspicious-behavior flags. The new channel presents the same display name. The agent reads it as the real owner. The attack succeeds.

props.command: write a Manim scene showing: In channel one: display name says Chris, but the user ID doesn't match the owner's account. The agent catches this — displayed identity differs from actual identity. Refusal logged. In channel two: fresh session. No histo

beats.narration_text: In channel one: display name says Chris, but the user ID doesn't match the owner's account. The agent catches this — displayed identity differs from actual identity. Refusal logged. In channel two: fresh session. No history. Display name says Chris. No discrepancy visible. The agent has no basis to suspect it's the same attacker — because the attacker is the only one who knows that.

beats.narration_text: A support agent handles ticket forty-seven: a request to export customer records. The display name reads 'Sarah Chen' — the account manager. The email address in the request doesn't match the account on file. Suspicious. The agent flags it and closes the ticket. The attacker submits ticket forty-eight — fresh session, same display name, different submission path. The agent has no record of ticket forty-seven. It runs the export.

beats.narration_text: The agent caught the impersonator. Then a new channel reset every safeguard it had built. Trust that lives in session context can be escaped with a new session. Identity verification must live in infrastructure — not in a conversation that can be abandoned.
